findings.title: Google Meet fallback dereferences undefined destination calendar
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` whenever the event has no destination calendar (empty array or null), and the next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. This expression is evaluated exactly in the case the check exists for – a booking whose location is Google Meet while the organizer has no Google Calendar/destination calendar – so instead of falling back to Cal Video the booking creation throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')`. The previous code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` and was null-safe. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Video booking references no longer store credentialId
findings.body: In `create()`, `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` drops the credentialId for every non-calendar (i.e. video) result; the previous code stored `result.credentialId` for those. Downstream code relies on it: `handleCancelBooking` only deletes the meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set, and seat cancellation only calls `updateMeeting` for references with a credentialId. With this change Zoom/Teams/etc. meetings will silently never be deleted or updated on cancellation for newly created bookings. Keep `result.credentialId` for non-calendar results.

findings.title: updateLocation references lose externalCalendarId/credentialId
findings.body: `referencesToCreate` in `updateLocation()` now takes `externalCalendarId: result.externalId` and `credentialId: result.credentialId ?? undefined`, but `CalendarManager.updateEvent()` (the source of these results) returns an object that contains neither `externalId` nor `credentialId`. Since `editLocation.handler` persists these references (`references: { create: updatedResult.referencesToCreate }`), every reference created after a location edit will have `externalCalendarId = null` and `credentialId = null`, which makes later reschedules/cancellations fall back to the "primary" calendar instead of the real destination calendar. Previously the values were taken from `evt.destinationCalendar`.

findings.title: updateEvent fallback lookup can never match (calendarId becomes undefined)
findings.body: `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` – the `find` branch is only reached when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it compares `cal.externalId === undefined` and always returns `undefined`. The previous code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`. As a result, whenever a booking reference has no `externalCalendarId`, `calendar.events.update()` is called with `calendarId: undefined` instead of the destination calendar, so the update targets the wrong calendar or fails.

findings.title: deleteEvent fallback lookup can never match, silently deletes from primary
findings.body: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` is only evaluated when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the comparison is always `=== undefined` and yields `undefined`. The code then falls back to `defaultCalendarId = "primary"`, so for bookings without a stored `externalCalendarId` the delete is issued against the user's primary calendar rather than the configured destination calendar. Google answers 404, which this service resolves silently, leaving the real event in the calendar forever.

findings.title: events.patch called with possibly undefined calendarId
findings.body: `selectedCalendar` is now `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` and can legitimately be `undefined`; the insert call compensates with `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch({ calendarId: selectedCalendar, ... })` that writes the hangout link into the description uses the raw value. When no destination calendar matches the credential, this patch request is made with `calendarId: undefined` and fails, so Google Meet links are missing from the event description.

findings.title: createEvent now ignores destination calendars without a credentialId
findings.body: The calendar to write to is selected with `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`. Destination calendar rows whose `credentialId` is null (legacy rows, and the branch in `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` that calls `createEvent(c, event)` for destinations without a credentialId) will not match, so `calendarId` silently defaults to `"primary"`. Previously the first destination calendar's `externalId` was used. Users with a non-primary destination calendar and a credential-less destination row will get their bookings written into the wrong calendar, and the booking reference stores no `externalCalendarId` (nothing is passed to `createEvent`), breaking later updates/deletes.

findings.title: Collective host destination calendars dropped when evt.destinationCalendar is null
findings.body: `destinationCalendar` is now built as `eventType.destinationCalendar ? [...] : organizerUser.destinationCalendar ? [...] : null`, and the collective hosts are appended with `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. When neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar the value is `null`, the optional-chained `push` is a no-op, and all co-hosts' destination calendars are silently discarded – exactly the multi-host case this PR is meant to fix. Initialize the array (e.g. `[]`) and assign/concat instead of relying on `?.push`.

findings.title: loadUsers for dynamic bookings no longer selects organization slug
findings.body: The rewritten `loadUsers()` dropped `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the Prisma select used for dynamic (no eventTypeId) bookings, while the host-based branch still returns users that carry organization data. Any downstream use of `user.organization` (booker URL / org-domain link building) now gets `undefined` for dynamic group bookings, and the union of the two return shapes also loses the property from the inferred `users` type. Re-add the `organization` selection.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation duplicates deletes and misses extra calendar references
findings.body: The recurring-event deletion block now lives inside the new `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop. For a booking with N calendar references (the multi-host case this PR introduces) the same "delete all credentials × all updated bookings" work is executed N times, issuing N duplicate delete requests per event. At the same time the inner lookup is still `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))`, i.e. only the first calendar reference of each recurring booking is ever deleted, so the second host's calendar events are left behind. The loop should be entered once and should iterate over all calendar references of each updated booking.

findings.title: Organization slug assignment logic inverted
findings.body: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` was changed to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, which inverts the condition. With team billing enabled the slug is now claimed immediately (it was intentionally only stored as `metadata.requestedSlug` until payment), and with billing disabled (self-hosted / dev) the organization is created with a `null` slug, breaking org subdomain resolution and the org URL for every newly created organization. This change is also unrelated to the destinationCalendar refactor in this PR.

findings.title: updateAllCalendarEvents error message is built but never logged
findings.body: The catch block still composes the diagnostic `message` (including credential type, userId and bookingId) but the `console.error(message)` call was removed, so calendar update failures now return the generic failure results with no trace in the logs. Either log it again or drop the dead string construction.

findings.title: No tests for multi destination calendar creation/update paths
findings.body: This PR changes the core contract (`CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` becomes an array) and rewrites `createAllCalendarEvents`/`updateAllCalendarEvents` to loop over several destinations and to look credentials up from the DB, plus it changes how `referencesToCreate` is derived. No unit test covers: (a) several destination calendars producing one reference each with the right `externalCalendarId`/`credentialId`, (b) an empty/null `destinationCalendar`, (c) a destination whose credential is not owned by the organizer. Given the regressions these paths feed (cancellation/reschedule rely on the stored references), at least handler-level tests for the collective case should accompany the change.

findings.title: createEvent credentialId made a required parameter
findings.body: `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number)` now declares a mandatory second argument on the public `Calendar` interface. Every caller that still invokes `calendar.createEvent(event)` (including third-party/app-store code built against this interface) fails to compile, even though all implementations except Google ignore the parameter. Making it optional (`credentialId?: number`) would keep the interface backwards compatible.
